# ImportSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ImportSection.html

`pub struct ImportSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the import section of WebAssembly modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{MemoryType, Module, ImportSection};
let mut imports = ImportSection::new();
imports.import(
    "env",
    "memory",
    MemoryType {
        minimum: 1,
        maximum: None,
        memory64: false,
        shared: false,
        page_size_log2: None,
    }
);
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&imports);
let bytes = module.finish();
```

# wasm_encoder::reencode - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/reencode/index.html

Available on

**crate feature**only.`wasmparser`## Expand description

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [component_](https://docs.rs/component_utils/index.html)- utils - `component-model`
- [utils](https://docs.rs/utils/index.html)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Roundtrip](https://docs.rs/struct.RoundtripReencoder.html)- Reencoder
- Reencodes `wasmparser`into`wasm-encoder`so that the encoded wasm is identical to the input and can be parsed and encoded again.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- An error when re-encoding from `wasmparser`to`wasm-encoder`.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Reencode](https://docs.rs/trait.Reencode.html)
- [Reencode](https://docs.rs/trait.ReencodeComponent.html)- Component - `component-model`

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/reencode.rs.html#508-515)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/reencode.rs.html#534-541)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/reencode.rs.html#534-541)

A hook method that is called inside [ Reencode::parse_core_module](https://docs.rs/trait.Reencode.html#method.parse_core_module)
before and after every non-custom core wasm section.

This method can be used to insert new custom sections in between those
sections, or to detect when a non-custom section is missing and insert
it in the [proper order](https://webassembly.github.io/spec/core/binary/modules.html#binary-module).

The `after` parameter is `None` iff the hook is called before the first
non-custom section, and `Some(s)` afterwards, where `s` is the
[ SectionId](https://docs.rs/enum.SectionId.html) of the previous non-custom section.

The `before` parameter is `None` iff the hook is called after the last
non-custom section, and `Some(s)` beforehand, where `s` is the
[ SectionId](https://docs.rs/enum.SectionId.html) of the following non-custom section.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/reencode.rs.html#543-550)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/reencode.rs.html#552-557)

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.BranchHints.html

`pub struct BranchHints { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Helper structure to encode the `metadata.code.branch_hint` custom section.

This section was defined in the branch-hinting proposal for WebAssembly:
[https://github.com/WebAssembly/branch-hinting](https://github.com/WebAssembly/branch-hinting).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::*;
let mut module = Module::new();
let mut types = TypeSection::new();
types.ty().function([], []);
module.section(&types);
let mut funcs = FunctionSection::new();
funcs.function(0);
module.section(&funcs);
let mut code = CodeSection::new();
let mut body = Function::new([]);
body.instructions().i32_const(1);
let if_offset = body.byte_len();
body.instructions()
    .if_(BlockType::Empty)
    .end()
    .end();
code.function(&body);
let mut hints = BranchHints::new();
hints.function_hints(0, [BranchHint {
    branch_func_offset: if_offset as u32,
    branch_hint_value: 1, // taken
}]);
module.section(&hints);
module.section(&code);
let wasm = module.finish();
let wat = wasmprinter::print_bytes(&wasm).unwrap();
assert_eq!(wat, r#"(module
  (type (;0;) (func))
  (func (;0;) (type 0)
    i32.const 1
    (@metadata.code.branch_hint "\01")
    if ;; label = @1
    end
  )
)
"#);
```

# CanonicalFunctionSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.CanonicalFunctionSection.html

`pub struct CanonicalFunctionSection { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`component-model`## Expand description

An encoder for the canonical function section of WebAssembly components.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Component, CanonicalFunctionSection, CanonicalOption};
let mut functions = CanonicalFunctionSection::new();
functions.lift(0, 0, [CanonicalOption::UTF8]);
let mut component = Component::new();
component.section(&functions);
let bytes = component.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# CodeSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.CodeSection.html

`pub struct CodeSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the code section.

Code sections are only supported for modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{
    CodeSection, Function, FunctionSection, Module,
    TypeSection, ValType
};
let mut types = TypeSection::new();
types.ty().function(vec![], vec![ValType::I32]);
let mut functions = FunctionSection::new();
let type_index = 0;
functions.function(type_index);
let locals = vec![];
let mut func = Function::new(locals);
func.instructions().i32_const(42);
let mut code = CodeSection::new();
code.function(&func);
let mut module = Module::new();
module
    .section(&types)
    .section(&functions)
    .section(&code);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#47-110)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-CodeSection)### impl [CodeSection](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeSection.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#47-110)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-CodeSection)

### impl [CodeSection](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeSection.html)

The number of bytes already added to this section.

This number doesn’t include the vector length that precedes the code entries, since it has a variable size that isn’t known until all functions are added.

Write a function body into this code section.

Add a raw byte slice into this code section as a function body.

The length prefix of the function body will be automatically prepended, and should not be included in the raw byte slice.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

You can use the `raw` method to copy an already-encoded function body
into a new code section encoder:

```
//                  id, size, # entries, entry
let code_section = [10, 6,    1,         4, 0, 65, 0, 11];
// Parse the code section.
let reader = BinaryReader::new(&code_section, 0);
let reader = CodeSectionReader::new(reader).unwrap();
let body = reader.into_iter().next().unwrap().unwrap();
let body_range = body.range();
// Add the body to a new code section encoder by copying bytes rather
// than re-parsing and re-encoding it.
let mut encoder = wasm_encoder::CodeSection::new();
encoder.raw(&code_section[body_range.start..body_range.end]);
```

# ComponentAliasSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ComponentAliasSection.html

`pub struct ComponentAliasSection { /* private fields */ }`Available on

**crate feature**only.`component-model`## Expand description

An encoder for the alias section of WebAssembly component.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Component, Alias, ComponentAliasSection, ComponentExportKind, ComponentOuterAliasKind};
let mut aliases = ComponentAliasSection::new();
aliases.alias(Alias::InstanceExport { instance: 0, kind: ComponentExportKind::Func, name: "f" });
aliases.alias(Alias::Outer { count: 0, kind: ComponentOuterAliasKind::Type, index: 1 });
let mut component = Component::new();
component.section(&aliases);
let bytes = component.finish();
```

# ComponentBuilder in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ComponentBuilder.html

`pub struct ComponentBuilder { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`component-model`## Expand description

Convenience type to build a component incrementally and automatically keep track of index spaces.

This type is intended to be a wrapper around the [ Component](https://docs.rs/struct.Component.html) encoding type
which is useful for building it up incrementally over time. This type will
automatically collect definitions into sections and reports the index of all
items added by keeping track of indices internally.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Completes this component and returns the binary encoding of the entire component.

Encodes a core wasm `Module` into this component, returning its index.

Encodes a core wasm `module` into this component, returning its index.

# ComponentExportSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ComponentExportSection.html

`pub struct ComponentExportSection { /* private fields */ }`Available on

**crate feature**only.`component-model`## Expand description

An encoder for the export section of WebAssembly component.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Component, ComponentExportSection, ComponentExportKind};
// This exports a function named "foo"
let mut exports = ComponentExportSection::new();
exports.export("foo", ComponentExportKind::Func, 0, None);
let mut component = Component::new();
component.section(&exports);
let bytes = component.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Used to encode component function types.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/component/types.rs.html#375-451)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-ComponentFuncTypeEncoder%3C'a%3E)### impl<'a> [ComponentFuncTypeEncoder](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentFuncTypeEncoder.html)<'a>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/component/types.rs.html#375-451)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-ComponentFuncTypeEncoder%3C'a%3E)

### impl<'a> [ComponentFuncTypeEncoder](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentFuncTypeEncoder.html)<'a>

Indicates whether this is an `async` function or not.

If this function is not invoked then the function type will not be
`async`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This method will panic if parameters or results have already been encoded.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/component/types.rs.html#443-450)#### pub fn [result](https://docs.rs#method.result)(&mut self, ty: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ComponentValType](https://docs.rs/enum.ComponentValType.html)>) -> &mut Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/component/types.rs.html#443-450)

#### pub fn [result](https://docs.rs#method.result)(&mut self, ty: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ComponentValType](https://docs.rs/enum.ComponentValType.html)>) -> &mut Self

Defines a single unnamed result.

This method cannot be used with `results`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

This method will panic if the function is called twice, called before
the `params` method, or called in addition to the `results` method.

# ComponentImportSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ComponentImportSection.html

`pub struct ComponentImportSection { /* private fields */ }`Available on

**crate feature**only.`component-model`## Expand description

An encoder for the import section of WebAssembly components.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Component, ComponentTypeSection, PrimitiveValType, ComponentImportSection, ComponentTypeRef};
let mut types = ComponentTypeSection::new();
// Define a function type of `[string, string] -> string`.
types
  .function()
  .params(
    [
      ("a", PrimitiveValType::String),
      ("b", PrimitiveValType::String)
    ]
  )
  .result(Some(PrimitiveValType::String.into()));
// This imports a function named `f` with the type defined above
let mut imports = ComponentImportSection::new();
imports.import("f", ComponentTypeRef::Func(0));
let mut component = Component::new();
component.section(&types);
component.section(&imports);
let bytes = component.finish();
```

# ComponentInstanceSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

`pub struct ComponentInstanceSection { /* private fields */ }`Available on

**crate feature**only.`component-model`## Expand description

An encoder for the instance section of WebAssembly components.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Component, ComponentInstanceSection, ComponentExportKind};
let mut instances = ComponentInstanceSection::new();
instances.export_items([("foo", ComponentExportKind::Func, 0)]);
instances.instantiate(1, [("foo", ComponentExportKind::Instance, 0)]);
let mut component = Component::new();
component.section(&instances);
let bytes = component.finish();
```

# ComponentNameSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ComponentNameSection.html

`pub struct ComponentNameSection { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`component-model`## Expand description

Encoding for the `component-name` custom section which assigns
human-readable names to items within a component.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Appends a component name subsection to this section.

This will indicate that the name of the entire component should be the
`name` specified. Note that this should be encoded first before other
subsections.

# ComponentStartSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ComponentStartSection.html

**crate feature**only.

`component-model`## Expand description

An encoder for the start section of WebAssembly components.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Component, ComponentStartSection};
let start = ComponentStartSection { function_index: 0, args: [0, 1], results: 1 };
let mut component = Component::new();
component.section(&start);
let bytes = component.finish();
```
## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.function_index)

`function_index: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The index to the start function.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.args)

`args: A`The arguments to pass to the start function.

An argument is an index to a value.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.results)

`results: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The number of expected results for the start function.

This should match the number of results for the type of
the function referenced by `function_index`.

# ComponentTypeSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ComponentTypeSection.html

`pub struct ComponentTypeSection { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`component-model`## Expand description

An encoder for the type section of WebAssembly components.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Component, ComponentTypeSection, PrimitiveValType};
let mut types = ComponentTypeSection::new();
// Define a function type of `[string, string] -> string`.
types
  .function()
  .params(
    [
      ("a", PrimitiveValType::String),
      ("b", PrimitiveValType::String)
    ]
  )
  .result(Some(PrimitiveValType::String.into()));
let mut component = Component::new();
component.section(&types);
let bytes = component.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# Struct ContType

[Source](../src/wasm_encoder/core/types.rs.html#101) `pub struct ContType(pub `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html));

## Expand description

Represents a type of a continuation in a WebAssembly module.

Performs copy-assignment from

`source`.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#method.clone_from)

Formats the value using the given formatter.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Debug.html#tymethod.fmt)

Tests for `self` and `other` values to be equal, and is used by `==`.

Tests for `!=`. The default implementation is almost always sufficient,
and should not be overridden without very good reason.

Immutably borrows from an owned value.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/borrow/trait.Borrow.html#tymethod.borrow)

Mutably borrows from an owned value.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/borrow/trait.BorrowMut.html#tymethod.borrow_mut)

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`clone_to_uninit`)

Performs copy-assignment from

`self` to

`dest`.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.CloneToUninit.html#tymethod.clone_to_uninit)

Returns the argument unchanged.

Calls `U::from(self)`.

That is, this conversion is whatever the implementation of
[From](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)<T> for U

The resulting type after obtaining ownership.

Creates owned data from borrowed data, usually by cloning.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/borrow/trait.ToOwned.html#tymethod.to_owned)

Uses borrowed data to replace owned data, usually by cloning.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/borrow/trait.ToOwned.html#method.clone_into)

The type returned in the event of a conversion error.

Performs the conversion.

# CoreDumpSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.CoreDumpSection.html

`pub struct CoreDumpSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The “core” custom section for coredumps, as described in the
[tool-conventions
repository](https://github.com/WebAssembly/tool-conventions/blob/main/Coredump.md).

There are four sections that comprise a core dump: - “core”, which contains the name of the core dump - “coremodules”, a listing of modules - “coreinstances”, a listing of module instances - “corestack”, a listing of frames for a specific thread

[§](https://docs.rs#example-of-how-these-could-be-constructed-and-encoded-into-a-module)Example of how these could be constructed and encoded into a module:

```
use wasm_encoder::{
    CoreDumpInstancesSection, CoreDumpModulesSection, CoreDumpSection, CoreDumpStackSection,
    CoreDumpValue, Module,
};
let core = CoreDumpSection::new("MyModule.wasm");
let mut modules = CoreDumpModulesSection::new();
modules.module("my_module");
let mut instances = CoreDumpInstancesSection::new();
let module_idx = 0;
let memories = vec![1];
let globals = vec![2];
instances.instance(module_idx, memories, globals);
let mut thread = CoreDumpStackSection::new("main");
let instance_index = 0;
let func_index = 42;
let code_offset = 0x1234;
let locals = vec![CoreDumpValue::I32(1)];
let stack = vec![CoreDumpValue::I32(2)];
thread.frame(instance_index, func_index, code_offset, locals, stack);
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&core);
module.section(&modules);
module.section(&instances);
module.section(&thread);
```

# CoreDumpStackSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.CoreDumpStackSection.html

`pub struct CoreDumpStackSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A “corestack” custom section as described in the [tool-conventions
repository](https://github.com/WebAssembly/tool-conventions/blob/main/Coredump.md)

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{CoreDumpStackSection, Module, CoreDumpValue};
let mut thread = CoreDumpStackSection::new("main");
let instance_index = 0;
let func_index = 42;
let code_offset = 0x1234;
let locals = vec![CoreDumpValue::I32(1)];
let stack = vec![CoreDumpValue::I32(2)];
thread.frame(instance_index, func_index, code_offset, locals, stack);
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&thread);
```

**crate feature**only.`component-model`## Expand description

An encoder for the core type section of WebAssembly components.

```
use wasm_encoder::{Component, CoreTypeSection, ModuleType};
let mut types = CoreTypeSection::new();
types.ty().module(&ModuleType::new());
let mut component = Component::new();
component.section(&types);

```

# DataSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.DataSection.html

`pub struct DataSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the data section.

Data sections are only supported for modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{
    ConstExpr, DataSection, Instruction, MemorySection, MemoryType,
    Module,
};
let mut memory = MemorySection::new();
memory.memory(MemoryType {
    minimum: 1,
    maximum: None,
    memory64: false,
    shared: false,
    page_size_log2: None,
});
let mut data = DataSection::new();
let memory_index = 0;
let offset = ConstExpr::i32_const(42);
let segment_data = b"hello";
data.active(memory_index, &offset, segment_data.iter().copied());
let mut module = Module::new();
module
    .section(&memory)
    .section(&data);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# DataSymbolDefinition in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.DataSymbolDefinition.html

## Expand description

The definition of a data symbol within a symbol table.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.index)

`index: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The index of the data segment that this symbol is in.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.offset)

`offset: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The offset of this symbol within its segment.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.size)

`size: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The byte size (which can be zero) of this data symbol.

Note that `offset + size` must be less than or equal to the segment’s
size.

# ElementSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ElementSection.html

`pub struct ElementSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the element section.

Element sections are only supported for modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use std::borrow::Cow;
use wasm_encoder::{
    Elements, ElementSection, Module, TableSection, TableType,
    RefType, ConstExpr
};
let mut tables = TableSection::new();
tables.table(TableType {
    element_type: RefType::FUNCREF,
    minimum: 128,
    maximum: None,
    table64: false,
    shared: false,
});
let mut elements = ElementSection::new();
let table_index = 0;
let offset = ConstExpr::i32_const(42);
let functions = Elements::Functions(Cow::Borrowed(&[
    // Function indices...
]));
elements.active(Some(table_index), &offset, functions);
let mut module = Module::new();
module
    .section(&tables)
    .section(&elements);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/elements.rs.html#107-165)#### pub fn [segment](https://docs.rs#method.segment)<'a>(&mut self, segment: [ElementSegment](https://docs.rs/struct.ElementSegment.html)<'a>) -> &mut Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/elements.rs.html#107-165)

#### pub fn [segment](https://docs.rs#method.segment)<'a>(&mut self, segment: [ElementSegment](https://docs.rs/struct.ElementSegment.html)<'a>) -> &mut Self

Define an element segment.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/elements.rs.html#172-185)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/elements.rs.html#172-185)

Define an active element segment.

`Active` element specifying a `None` table forces the MVP encoding and refers to the 0th
table holding `funcref`s. Non-`None` tables use the encoding introduced with the bulk
memory proposal and can refer to tables with any valid reference type.

Encode a passive element segment.

Passive segments are part of the bulk memory proposal.

# Function in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.Function.html

`pub struct Function { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for a function body within the code section.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{CodeSection, Function};
// Define the function body for:
//
//     (func (param i32 i32) (result i32)
//       local.get 0
//       local.get 1
//       i32.add)
let locals = vec![];
let mut func = Function::new(locals);
func.instructions()
    .local_get(0)
    .local_get(1)
    .i32_add();
// Add our function to the code section.
let mut code = CodeSection::new();
code.function(&func);
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Create a new function body with the given locals.

The argument is an iterator over `(N, Ty)`, which defines
that the next `N` locals will be of type `Ty`.

For example, a function with locals 0 and 1 of type I32 and local 2 of type F32 would be created as:

`let f = Function::new([(2, ValType::I32), (1, ValType::F32)]);`For more information about the code section (and function definition) in the WASM binary format
see the [WebAssembly spec](https://webassembly.github.io/spec/core/binary/modules.html#binary-func)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#200-220)#### pub fn [new_with_locals_types](https://docs.rs#method.new_with_locals_types)<L>(locals: L) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#200-220)

#### pub fn [new_with_locals_types](https://docs.rs#method.new_with_locals_types)<L>(locals: L) -> Self

Create a function from a list of locals’ types.

Unlike [ Function::new](https://docs.rs/struct.Function.html#method.new), this constructor simply takes a list of types
which are in order associated with locals.

For example:

```
let f = Function::new([(2, ValType::I32), (1, ValType::F32)]);
let g = Function::new_with_locals_types([
   ValType::I32, ValType::I32, ValType::F32
]);
assert_eq!(f, g)
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#223-225)#### pub fn [instructions](https://docs.rs#method.instructions)(&mut self) -> [InstructionSink](https://docs.rs/struct.InstructionSink.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#223-225)

#### pub fn [instructions](https://docs.rs#method.instructions)(&mut self) -> [InstructionSink](https://docs.rs/struct.InstructionSink.html)<'_>

Get an instruction encoder for this function body.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#228-231)#### pub fn [instruction](https://docs.rs#method.instruction)(&mut self, instruction: &[Instruction](https://docs.rs/enum.Instruction.html)<'_>) -> &mut Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#228-231)

#### pub fn [instruction](https://docs.rs#method.instruction)(&mut self, instruction: &[Instruction](https://docs.rs/enum.Instruction.html)<'_>) -> &mut Self

Write an instruction into this function body.

The number of bytes already added to this function.

This number doesn’t include the variable-width size field that `encode`
will write before the added bytes, since the size of that field isn’t
known until all the instructions are added to this function.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#286-288)#### pub fn [into_raw_body](https://docs.rs#method.into_raw_body)(self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/code.rs.html#286-288)

#### pub fn [into_raw_body](https://docs.rs#method.into_raw_body)(self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Unwraps and returns the raw byte encoding of this function.

This encoding doesn’t include the variable-width size field
that `encode` will write before the added bytes. As such, its
length will match the return value of [ Function::byte_len](https://docs.rs/struct.Function.html#method.byte_len).

[§](https://docs.rs#use-case)Use Case

This raw byte form is suitable for later using with
[ CodeSection::raw](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeSection.html#method.raw). Note that it

*differs*from what results from

[precisely due to the](https://docs.rs/struct.Function.html#method.encode)

`Function::encode`*lack*of the length prefix;

[will use this. Using](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeSection.html#method.raw)

`CodeSection::raw`[instead produces bytes that cannot be fed into other wasm-encoder types without stripping off the length prefix, which is awkward and error-prone.](https://docs.rs/struct.Function.html#method.encode)

`Function::encode`This method combined with [ CodeSection::raw](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeSection.html#method.raw) may be useful
together if one wants to save the result of function encoding
and use it later: for example, caching the result of some code
generation process.

For example:

```
let mut f = Function::new([]);
f.instructions().end();
let bytes = f.into_raw_body();
// (save `bytes` somewhere for later use)
let mut code = CodeSection::new();
code.raw(&bytes[..]);
assert_eq!(2, bytes.len());  // Locals count, then `end`
assert_eq!(3, code.byte_len()); // Function length byte, function body
```

# FunctionSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

`pub struct FunctionSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the function section of WebAssembly modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Module, FunctionSection, ValType};
let mut functions = FunctionSection::new();

module.section(&functions);

# GlobalSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.GlobalSection.html

`pub struct GlobalSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the global section.

Global sections are only supported for modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{ConstExpr, Module, GlobalSection, GlobalType, Instruction, ValType};
let mut globals = GlobalSection::new();
globals.global(
    GlobalType {
        val_type: ValType::I32,
        mutable: false,
        shared: false,
    },
    &ConstExpr::i32_const(42),
);
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&globals);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

## Expand description

A map used to describe names with two levels of indirection, as opposed to a
`NameMap`

This naming map is used with `NameSection::locals`

Creates a new empty name map.

Adds a new entry where the item at `idx` has sub-items named within
`names` as specified.

For example if this is describing local names then `idx` is a function
index where the indexes within `names` are local indices.

`source`.

Encode the type into the given byte sink.

# NameMap in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.NameMap.html

`pub struct NameMap { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Adds a an entry where the item at `idx` has the `name` specified.

Note that indices should be appended in ascending order of the index
value. Each index may only be named once, but not all indices must be
named (e.g. `0 foo; 1 bar; 7 qux` is valid but `0 foo; 0 bar` is not).
Names do not have to be unique (e.g. `0 foo; 1 foo; 2 foo` is valid).

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

# InstanceSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.InstanceSection.html

`pub struct InstanceSection { /* private fields */ }`Available on

**crate feature**only.`component-model`## Expand description

An encoder for the core instance section of WebAssembly components.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Component, InstanceSection, ExportKind, ModuleArg};
let mut instances = InstanceSection::new();
instances.export_items([("foo", ExportKind::Func, 0)]);
instances.instantiate(1, [("foo", ModuleArg::Instance(0))]);
let mut component = Component::new();
component.section(&instances);
let bytes = component.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# LinkingSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.LinkingSection.html

`pub struct LinkingSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the [linking custom
section](https://github.com/WebAssembly/tool-conventions/blob/master/Linking.md#linking-metadata-section).

This section is a non-standard convention that is supported by the LLVM toolchain. It, along with associated “reloc.*” custom sections, allows you to treat a Wasm module as a low-level object file that can be linked with other Wasm object files to produce a final, complete Wasm module.

The linking section must come before the reloc sections.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{LinkingSection, Module, SymbolTable};
// Create a new linking section.
let mut linking = LinkingSection::new();
// Define a symbol table.
let mut sym_tab = SymbolTable::new();
// Define a function symbol in the symbol table.
let flags = SymbolTable::WASM_SYM_BINDING_LOCAL | SymbolTable::WASM_SYM_EXPORTED;
let func_index = 42;
let sym_name = "my_exported_func";
sym_tab.function(flags, func_index, Some(sym_name));
// Add the symbol table to our linking section.
linking.symbol_table(&sym_tab);
// Add the linking section to a new Wasm module and get the encoded bytes.
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&linking);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```

# MemArg in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.MemArg.html

## Expand description

The immediate for a memory instruction.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.offset)

`offset: `[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)A static offset to add to the instruction’s dynamic address operand.

This is a `u64` field for the memory64 proposal, but 32-bit memories
limit offsets to at most `u32::MAX` bytes. This will be encoded as a LEB
but it won’t generate a valid module if an offset is specified which is
larger than the maximum size of the index space for the memory indicated
by `memory_index`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.align)

`align: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The expected alignment of the instruction’s dynamic address operand (expressed the exponent of a power of two).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.memory_index)

`memory_index: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The index of the memory this instruction is operating upon.

# MemorySection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.MemorySection.html

`pub struct MemorySection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the memory section.

Memory sections are only supported for modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Module, MemorySection, MemoryType};
let mut memories = MemorySection::new();
memories.memory(MemoryType {
    minimum: 1,
    maximum: None,
    memory64: false,
    shared: false,
    page_size_log2: None,
});
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&memories);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```

# MemoryType in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.MemoryType.html

```
pub struct MemoryType {
    pub minimum:
```
[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html),
    pub maximum: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)>,
    pub memory64: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub shared: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub page_size_log2: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>,
}## Expand description

A memory’s type.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.minimum)

`minimum: `[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)Minimum size, in pages, of this memory

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.maximum)

`maximum: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)>Maximum size, in pages, of this memory

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.memory64)

`memory64: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether or not this is a 64-bit memory.

Whether or not this memory is shared.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.page_size_log2)

`page_size_log2: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>The log base 2 of a custom page size for this memory.

The default page size for Wasm memories is 64KiB, i.e. 216 or
`65536`.

After the introduction of [the custom-page-sizes
proposal](https://github.com/WebAssembly/custom-page-sizes), Wasm can
customize the page size. It must be a power of two that is less than or
equal to 64KiB. Attempting to encode an invalid page size may panic.

# NameSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.NameSection.html

`pub struct NameSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the custom `name` section.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Module, NameSection, NameMap};
let mut names = NameSection::new();
names.module("the module name");
let mut function_names = NameMap::new();
function_names.append(0, "name of function 0");
function_names.append(1, "a better function");
function_names.append(3, "the best function");
names.functions(&function_names);
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&names);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/names.rs.html#56-202)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-NameSection)### impl [NameSection](https://docs.rs/struct.NameSection.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/names.rs.html#56-202)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-NameSection)

### impl [NameSection](https://docs.rs/struct.NameSection.html)

Appends a module name subsection to this section.

This will indicate that the name of the entire module should be the
`name` specified. Note that this should be encoded first before other
subsections.

Appends a subsection for the names of all functions in this wasm module.

Function names are declared in the `names` map provided where the index
in the map corresponds to the wasm index of the function. This section
should come after the module name subsection (if present) and before the
locals subsection (if present).

# ProducersSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.ProducersSection.html

`pub struct ProducersSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the [producers custom
section](https://github.com/WebAssembly/tool-conventions/blob/main/ProducersSection.md).

This section is a non-standard convention that is supported by many toolchains.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{ProducersSection, ProducersField, Module};
// Create a new producers section.
let mut field = ProducersField::new();
field.value("clang", "14.0.4");
field.value("rustc", "1.66.1 (90743e729 2023-01-10)");
let mut producers = ProducersSection::new();
producers.field("processed-by", &field);
// Add the producers section to a new Wasm module and get the encoded bytes.
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&producers);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# StartSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.StartSection.html

```
pub struct StartSection {
    pub function_index:
```
[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
}## Expand description

An encoder for the start section of WebAssembly modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Note: this doesn’t actually define the function at index 0, its type, or its
code body, so the resulting Wasm module will be invalid. See `TypeSection`,
`FunctionSection`, and `CodeSection` for details on how to generate those
things.

```
use wasm_encoder::{Module, StartSection};
let start = StartSection { function_index: 0 };
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&start);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```
## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

`function_index: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The index of the start function.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#202)#### pub const [WASM_SYM_BINDING_WEAK](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_BINDING_WEAK): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x1

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#202)

#### pub const [WASM_SYM_BINDING_WEAK](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_BINDING_WEAK): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x1

This is a weak symbol.

This flag is mutually exclusive with `WASM_SYM_BINDING_LOCAL`.

When linking multiple modules defining the same symbol, all weak definitions are discarded if any strong definitions exist; then if multiple weak definitions exist all but one (unspecified) are discarded; and finally it is an error if more than one definition remains.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#212)#### pub const [WASM_SYM_BINDING_LOCAL](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_BINDING_LOCAL): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x02

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#212)

#### pub const [WASM_SYM_BINDING_LOCAL](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_BINDING_LOCAL): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x02

This is a local symbol.

This flag is mutually exclusive with `WASM_SYM_BINDING_WEAK`.

Local symbols are not to be exported, or linked to other modules/sections. The names of all non-local symbols must be unique, but the names of local symbols are not considered for uniqueness. A local function or global symbol cannot reference an import.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#218)#### pub const [WASM_SYM_VISIBILITY_HIDDEN](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_VISIBILITY_HIDDEN): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x04

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#218)

#### pub const [WASM_SYM_VISIBILITY_HIDDEN](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_VISIBILITY_HIDDEN): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x04

This is a hidden symbol.

Hidden symbols are not to be exported when performing the final link, but may be linked to other modules.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#224)#### pub const [WASM_SYM_UNDEFINED](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_UNDEFINED): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x10

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#224)

#### pub const [WASM_SYM_UNDEFINED](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_UNDEFINED): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x10

This symbol is not defined.

For non-data symbols, this must match whether the symbol is an import or is defined; for data symbols, determines whether a segment is specified.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#231)#### pub const [WASM_SYM_EXPORTED](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_EXPORTED): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x20

#### pub const [WASM_SYM_EXPORTED](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_EXPORTED): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x20

This symbol is intended to be exported from the wasm module to the host environment.

This differs from the visibility flags in that it effects the static linker.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasm_encoder/core/linking.rs.html#238)#### pub const [WASM_SYM_EXPLICIT_NAME](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.WASM_SYM_EXPLICIT_NAME): [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 0x40

This symbol uses an explicit symbol name, rather than reusing the name from a wasm import.

This allows it to remap imports from foreign WebAssembly modules into local symbols with different names.

# TableSection in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/struct.TableSection.html

`pub struct TableSection { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An encoder for the table section.

Table sections are only supported for modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use wasm_encoder::{Module, TableSection, TableType, RefType};
let mut tables = TableSection::new();
tables.table(TableType {
    element_type: RefType::FUNCREF,
    minimum: 128,
    maximum: None,
    table64: false,
    shared: false,
});
let mut module = Module::new();
module.section(&tables);
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
```

### Func

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Extern)

### Extern

The abstract external heap type.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Any)

### Any

The abstract `any` heap type.

The common supertype (a.k.a. top) of all internal types.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.None)

### None

The abstract `none` heap type.

The common subtype (a.k.a. bottom) of all internal types.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NoExtern)

### NoExtern

The abstract `noextern` heap type.

The common subtype (a.k.a. bottom) of all external types.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NoFunc)

### NoFunc

The abstract `nofunc` heap type.

The common subtype (a.k.a. bottom) of all function types.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Eq)

### Eq

The abstract `eq` heap type.

The common supertype of all referenceable types on which comparison (ref.eq) is allowed.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Struct)

### Struct

The abstract `struct` heap type.

The common supertype of all struct types.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Array)

### Array

The abstract `array` heap type.

The common supertype of all array types.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.I31)

### I31

The unboxed `i31` heap type.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Exn)

### Exn

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Cont)

# CanonicalOption in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/enum.CanonicalOption.html

```
pub enum CanonicalOption {
    UTF8,
    UTF16,
    CompactUTF16,
    Memory(
```
[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)),
    Realloc([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)),
    PostReturn([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)),
    Async,
    Callback([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)),
    CoreType([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)),
    Gc,
}**crate feature**only.

`component-model`## Expand description

Represents options for canonical function definitions.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UTF8)

### UTF8

The string types in the function signature are UTF-8 encoded.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UTF16)

### UTF16

The string types in the function signature are UTF-16 encoded.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CompactUTF16)

### CompactUTF16

The string types in the function signature are compact UTF-16 encoded.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Memory)

### Memory([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html))

The memory to use if the lifting or lowering of a function requires memory access.

The value is an index to a core memory.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Realloc)

### Realloc([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html))

The realloc function to use if the lifting or lowering of a function requires memory allocation.

The value is an index to a core function of type `(func (param i32 i32 i32 i32) (result i32))`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.PostReturn)

### PostReturn([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html))

The post-return function to use if the lifting of a function requires cleanup after the function returns.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Async)

### Async

Indicates that specified function should be lifted or lowered using the `async` ABI.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Callback)

### Callback([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html))

The function to use if the async lifting of a function should receive task/stream/future progress events using a callback.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CoreType)

### CoreType([u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html))

The core function type to lower a component function into.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Gc)

### Gc

Use the GC variant of the canonical ABI.

# ExportKind in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/enum.ExportKind.html

```
#[repr(u8)]pub enum ExportKind {
    Func = 0,
    Table = 1,
    Memory = 2,
    Global = 3,
    Tag = 4,
}
```
## Expand description

Represents the kind of an export from a WebAssembly module.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Func)

### Func = 0

The export is a function.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Table)

### Table = 1

The export is a table.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Memory)

### Memory = 2

The export is a memory.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Global)

### Global = 3

The export is a global.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Tag)

### Tag = 4

The export is a tag.

## Expand description

Part of the function references proposal.

An abstract heap type; e.g., `anyref`.

A concrete Wasm-defined type at the given index.

Alias for the unshared `any` heap type.

Alias for the unshared `func` heap type.

Alias for the unshared `extern` heap type.

Alias for the unshared `i31` heap type.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.

# Ordering in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/enum.Ordering.html

Enum Ordering  Copy item path  Source  ```
pub enum Ordering {
    AcqRel,
    SeqCst,
}
```
Expand description The memory ordering for atomic instructions.

For an in-depth explanation of memory orderings, see the C++ documentation
for `memory_order``atomic::Ordering`

For a load, it acquires; this orders all operations before the last
“releasing” store. For a store, it releases; this orders all operations
before it at the next “acquiring” load.

Like `AcqRel` but all threads see all sequentially consistent operations
in the same order.

Performs copy-assignment from

`source`.

Read more Formats the value using the given formatter.

Read more Encode the type into the given byte sink.

`self` to

`dest`.

`component-model`## Expand description

A WebAssembly component section.

Various builders defined in this crate already implement this trait, but you
can also implement it yourself for your own custom section builders, or use
`RawSection` to use a bunch of raw bytes as a section.

# Section in wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/0.252.0/wasm_encoder/trait.Section.html

`pub trait Section: `[Encode](https://docs.rs/trait.Encode.html) {
    // Required method
    fn [id](https://docs.rs#tymethod.id)(&self) -> [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html);
    // Provided method
    fn [append_to](https://docs.rs#method.append_to)(&self, dst: &mut [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>) { ... }
}## Expand description

A WebAssembly module section.

Various builders defined in this crate already implement this trait, but you
can also implement it yourself for your own custom section builders, or use
`RawSection` to use a bunch of raw bytes as a section.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# wasm_encoder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-encoder/latest/wasm_encoder/

## Expand description

A WebAssembly encoder.

The main builder is the [ Module](https://docs.rs/struct.Module.html). You can build a section with a
section-specific builder, like

[or](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeSection.html)

`TypeSection`[, and then add it to the module with](https://docs.rs/struct.ImportSection.html)

`ImportSection`[. When you are finished building the module, call either](https://docs.rs/struct.Module.html#method.section)

`Module::section`[or](https://docs.rs/struct.Module.html#method.as_slice)

`Module::as_slice`[to get the encoded bytes. The former gives a shared reference to the underlying bytes as a slice, while the latter gives you ownership of them as a vector.](https://docs.rs/struct.Module.html#method.finish)

`Module::finish`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

If we wanted to build this module:

```
(module
  (type (func (param i32 i32) (result i32)))
  (func (type 0)
    local.get 0
    local.get 1
    i32.add)
  (export "f" (func 0)))
```
then we would do this:

```
use wasm_encoder::{
    CodeSection, ExportKind, ExportSection, Function, FunctionSection,
    Module, TypeSection, ValType,
};
let mut module = Module::new();
// Encode the type section.
let mut types = TypeSection::new();
let params = vec![ValType::I32, ValType::I32];
let results = vec![ValType::I32];
types.ty().function(params, results);
module.section(&types);
// Encode the function section.
let mut functions = FunctionSection::new();
let type_index = 0;
functions.function(type_index);
module.section(&functions);
// Encode the export section.
let mut exports = ExportSection::new();
exports.export("f", ExportKind::Func, 0);
module.section(&exports);
// Encode the code section.
let mut codes = CodeSection::new();
let locals = vec![];
let mut f = Function::new(locals);
f.instructions()
    .local_get(0)
    .local_get(1)
    .i32_add()
    .end();
codes.function(&f);
module.section(&codes);
// Extract the encoded Wasm bytes for this module.
let wasm_bytes = module.finish();
// We generated a valid Wasm module!
assert!(wasmparser::validate(&wasm_bytes).is_ok());
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- A map used to name items in a wasm module, organized by naming each individual index.
- [Name](https://docs.rs/struct.NameSection.html)- Section
- An encoder for the custom `name`section.
- [Nested](https://docs.rs/struct.NestedComponentSection.html)- Component - Section - `component-model`
- An encoder for the component section of WebAssembly components.
- [Producers](https://docs.rs/struct.ProducersField.html)- Field
- The value of a field in the producers custom section
- [Producers](https://docs.rs/struct.ProducersSection.html)- Section
- An encoder for the [producers custom section](https://github.com/WebAssembly/tool-conventions/blob/main/ProducersSection.md).
- [RawCustom](https://docs.rs/struct.RawCustomSection.html)- Section
- A raw custom section where the bytes specified contain the leb-encoded length of the custom section, the custom section’s name, and the custom section’s data.
- [RawSection](https://docs.rs/struct.RawSection.html)
- A section made up of uninterpreted, raw bytes.
- [RefType](https://docs.rs/struct.RefType.html)
- A reference type.
- [Start](https://docs.rs/struct.StartSection.html)- Section
- An encoder for the start section of WebAssembly modules.
- [Struct](https://docs.rs/struct.StructType.html)- Type
- Represents a type of a struct in a WebAssembly module.
- [SubType](https://docs.rs/struct.SubType.html)
- Represents a subtype of possible other types in a WebAssembly module.
- [Symbol](https://docs.rs/struct.SymbolTable.html)- Table
- A subsection of the [linking custom section](https://docs.rs/struct.LinkingSection.html)that provides extra information about the symbols present in this Wasm object file.
- [Table](https://docs.rs/struct.TableSection.html)- Section
- An encoder for the table section.
- [Table](https://docs.rs/struct.TableType.html)- Type
- A table’s type.
- [TagSection](https://docs.rs/struct.TagSection.html)
- An encoder for the tag section.
- [TagType](https://docs.rs/struct.TagType.html)
- A tag’s type.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeSection.html)- Section
- An encoder for the type section of WebAssembly modules.

# leb128fmt 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/leb128fmt/^0.1.0

# Leb128fmt

Leb128fmt is a library to decode and encode [LEB128](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LEB128) formatted numbers.
LEB128 is a variable length integer compression format.

The library does not allocate memory and can be used in `no_std` and
`no_std::no_alloc` environments.

Various functions are provided which encode and decode signed and unsigned integers with the number of bits in the function name. There are generic functions provided to read and write slices of encoded values as well.

There are encoding functions with the word `fixed` in the name which will
write out a value using the maximum number of bytes for a given bit size.
For instance, using `encode_fixed_u32` will always use 5 bytes to
write out the value. While always using the maximum number of bytes removes
the benefit of compression, in some scenarios, it is beneficial to have a
fixed encoding size.

Finally, there are macros provided which you can use to build your own encoding and decoding functions for unusual variants like signed 33 bit values.

## Installation

```
```
## Examples

### Functions using Arrays

```
// Encode an unsigned 32 bit number:
let  = encode_u32.unwrap;
// The number of bytes written in the output array
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// The entire output array. Note you should only use &output[..written_len] to copy
// into your output buffer
assert_eq!;
// Decode an unsigned 32 bit number:
let input = ;
let  = decode_u32.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
#### Helper Functions

If you are reading from an input buffer, you can use `is_last` and
`max_len` to determine the bytes to copy into the array.

```
let buffer = vec!;
let pos = 2;
let end = buffer.iter.skip.copied.position.map;
if let Some = end  else
```
### Functions Using Slices

```
let mut buffer = vec!;
let mut pos = 1;
// Encode an unsigned 64 bit number with a mutable slice:
let result = ;
// The number of bytes written in the output array
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Decode an unsigned 64 bit number with a slice:
pos = 1;
let result = ;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Functions Using Fixed Sized Encoding

There may be several different ways to encode a value. For instance, `0` can
be encoded as 32 bits unsigned:

```
let mut pos = 0;
assert_eq!;
pos = 0;
assert_eq!;
pos = 0;
assert_eq!;
pos = 0;
assert_eq!;
pos = 0;
assert_eq!;
```
There are functions provided to encode a value using the maximum number of bytes possible for a given bit size. Using the maximum number of bytes removes the benefit of compression, but it may be useful in a few scenarios.

For instance, if a binary format needs to store the size or offset of some
data before the size of data is known, it can be beneficial to write a fixed
sized `0` placeholder value first. Then, once the real value is known, the
`0` placeholder can be overwritten without moving other bytes. The real
value is also written out using the fixed maximum number of bytes.

```
// Encode an unsigned 32 bit number with all 5 bytes:
let output  = encode_fixed_u32.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
// Decode an unsigned 32 bit number:
let input = output;
let  = decode_u32.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
// Note that all 5 bytes are read
assert_eq!;
```

License](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT) at your option.

# wasmparser 0.252.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasmparser/^0.252.0

`wasmparser`: A WebAssembly Binary Parser

**A  Bytecode Alliance project**

A simple, event-driven library for parsing WebAssembly binary files (or streams).

The library reports events as they happen and only stores parsing information for a brief period of time, making it fast and memory-efficient. The event-driven model, however, has some drawbacks. If you need random access to the entire WebAssembly data-structure, this is not the right library for you. You could however, build such a data-structure using this library.

To get started, create a
[ Parser](https://docs.rs/wasmparser/latest/wasmparser/struct.Parser.html)
using

[and then follow the examples documented for](https://docs.rs/wasmparser/latest/wasmparser/struct.Parser.html#method.new)

`Parser::new`[or](https://docs.rs/wasmparser/latest/wasmparser/struct.Parser.html#method.parse)

`Parser::parse`[.](https://docs.rs/wasmparser/latest/wasmparser/struct.Parser.html#method.parse_all)

`Parser::parse_all`## Documentation

Documentation and examples can be found at [https://docs.rs/wasmparser/](https://docs.rs/wasmparser/)

# anyhow 1.0.103 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/anyhow/^1.0.58

# Anyhow ¯\_(°ペ)_/¯

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0/anyhow/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error type
for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
## Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use Result;`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like "No such file or directory" can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use ;``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use Error;`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err;`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!;`

## No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled "std" feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0",  = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow's error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

## Comparison to failure

The `anyhow::Error` type works something like `failure::Error`, but unlike
failure ours is built around the standard library's `std::error::Error` trait
rather than a separate trait `failure::Fail`. The standard library has adopted
the necessary improvements for this to be possible as part of [RFC 2504](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/2504-fix-error.md).

## Comparison to thiserror

Use Anyhow if you don't care what error type your functions return, you just
want it to be easy. This is common in application code. Use [thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror) if you
are a library that wants to design your own dedicated error type(s) so that on
failures the caller gets exactly the information that you choose.

---

# tempfile 3.27.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/tempfile/^3.2.0

# tempfile

A secure, cross-platform, temporary file library for Rust. In addition to creating temporary files, this library also allows users to securely open multiple independent references to the same temporary file (useful for consumer/producer patterns and surprisingly difficult to implement securely).

## Usage

Minimum required Rust version: 1.63.0

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "3"
```
## Supported Platforms

This crate supports all major operating systems:

- Linux
- Android
- MacOS
- Windows
- FreeBSD (likely other BSDs but we don't have CI for them)
- RedoxOS
- Wasm (build and link only, Wasm doesn't have a filesystem)
- WASI P1 & P2.

However:

- Android, RedoxOS, Wasm, and WASI targets all require the latest stable rust compiler.
- WASI P1/P2 does not define a default temporary directory. You'll need to explicitly call `tempfile::env::override_temp_dir`with a valid directory or temporary file creation will panic on this platform.
- WASI P1/P2 does not have file permissions.
- You *may*need to override the temporary directory in Android as well to point at your application's per-app cache directory.

## Example

```
use File;
use ;
```

# wasm-encoder 0.251.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasm-encoder/0.251.0

A Bytecode Alliance project

## Usage

Add `wasm-encoder` to your `Cargo.toml`

```
```
And then you can encode WebAssembly binaries via:

```
use ;
let mut module = new;
// Encode the type section.
let mut types = new;
let params = vec!;
let results = vec!;
types.ty.function;
module.section;
// Encode the function section.
let mut functions = new;
let type_index = 0;
functions.function;
module.section;
// Encode the export section.
let mut exports = new;
exports.export;
module.section;
// Encode the code section.
let mut codes = new;
let locals = vec!;
let mut f = new;
f.instructions
    .local_get
    .local_get
    .i32_add
    .end;
codes.function;
module.section;
// Extract the encoded Wasm bytes for this module.
let wasm_bytes = module.finish;
// We generated a valid Wasm module!
assert!;
```

# wasm-encoder 0.246.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasm-encoder/0.246.0

A Bytecode Alliance project

## Usage

Add `wasm-encoder` to your `Cargo.toml`

```
```
And then you can encode WebAssembly binaries via:

```
use ;
let mut module = new;
// Encode the type section.
let mut types = new;
let params = vec!;
let results = vec!;
types.ty.function;
module.section;
// Encode the function section.
let mut functions = new;
let type_index = 0;
functions.function;
module.section;
// Encode the export section.
let mut exports = new;
exports.export;
module.section;
// Encode the code section.
let mut codes = new;
let locals = vec!;
let mut f = new;
f.instructions
    .local_get
    .local_get
    .i32_add
    .end;
codes.function;
module.section;
// Extract the encoded Wasm bytes for this module.
let wasm_bytes = module.finish;
// We generated a valid Wasm module!
assert!;
```
# License

This project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license with the LLVM exception.
See [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE) for more details.

### Contribution

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this project by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

# wasm-encoder 0.230.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasm-encoder/0.230.0

A Bytecode Alliance project

## Usage

Add `wasm-encoder` to your `Cargo.toml`

```
```
And then you can encode WebAssembly binaries via:

```
use ;
let mut module = new;
// Encode the type section.
let mut types = new;
let params = vec!;
let results = vec!;
types.ty.function;
module.section;
// Encode the function section.
let mut functions = new;
let type_index = 0;
functions.function;
module.section;
// Encode the export section.
let mut exports = new;
exports.export;
module.section;
// Encode the code section.
let mut codes = new;
let locals = vec!;
let mut f = new;
f.instructions
    .local_get
    .local_get
    .i32_add
    .end;
codes.function;
module.section;
// Extract the encoded Wasm bytes for this module.
let wasm_bytes = module.finish;
// We generated a valid Wasm module!
assert!;
```
# License

This project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license with the LLVM exception.
See [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE) for more details.

### Contribution

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this project by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.
